current_mapping_state.existing_rationale: sosa:observedProperty relates an Observation to the ObservableProperty it observes. No satisfactory existing BFO/CCO/RO superproperty has been identified that captures this relationship without introducing unwanted participation or input semantics. ObservableProperties can be specifically dependent continuants or occurrent process profiles. The existing sosa:ObservableProperty class mapping accommodates both. The source-class domain and range axioms make classifications logically enforceable through OWL inference. They do not, by themselves, establish that the property belongs to the same FeatureOfInterest associated with the Observation. These are global OWL typing commitments, not SHACL validation constraints. This explicit human-approved typing treatment supersedes the earlier technical deferral as the current treatment; the historical deferral and its former input interpretation remain preserved as evidence. The previously removed sosa:observedProperty rdfs:subPropertyOf cco:has_input is not restored, and no BFO, CCO, or RO superproperty is introduced.

derived_consequences.explanation: Every property subject belongs to the declared domain or one of its union branches; each branch restricts all values of this property to the stated class. Thus every object has that type. This derived consequence is separate from an explicit range assertion and makes no mapping decision.

formal_consequences: An asserted sosa:observedProperty(x,y) types x as sosa:Observation; no BFO/CCO relation edge is entailed by this typing axiom alone.
An asserted sosa:observedProperty(x,y) types y as sosa:ObservableProperty; no BFO/CCO relation edge is entailed by this typing axiom alone.

pinned_track_comparison.rationale: No direct BFO/CCO object-property mapping is adopted. sosa:observedProperty relates an Observation or ObservationCollection to the Property observed. CCO has input requires an Independent Continuant input whose presence at the beginning is necessary for a Process to start, which is not entailed by observation and does not cover the ProcessProfile branch of sosa:Property. CCO aboutness relations instead require an Information Content Entity subject. No reviewed BFO/CCO relation provides the required uniform semantics.

definitions: Relation linking an Observation to the property that was observed. The ObservableProperty should be a property of the FeatureOfInterest (linked by hasFeatureOfInterest) of this Observation.
